notes:
Compatibility reports now find your game even if you renamed the file.

Until now the compatibility database matched games by file name on every system
except GameCube and Wii. If your copy of a game was named even slightly
differently, the pre-launch Compatibility panel found nothing and told you to be
the first to report it, when in fact the game already had reports.

Reports are now filed against the game itself, read out of the ROM. PlayStation,
PS2 and PSP use the disc serial, Dreamcast its product number, 3DS and Wii U
their title id, and N64, DS and GBA their cart code. NES, SNES, Game Boy and
Genesis carry no id inside them, so the ROM itself is fingerprinted instead.
GameCube and Wii already worked this way and are unchanged.

Nothing is lost in the move. The first time anyone reports a game under its new
identity, every older report for that game moves across with it, for everyone.
A game nobody has reported since this update keeps matching on its file name
until someone does.

Your console reads these identities in the background shortly after it starts,
so opening the Compatibility panel stays instant.

PSP games in .pbp or .cso format, and plain .iso or .bin disc images, have not
been tested. If one cannot be read, that game simply falls back to matching by
name exactly as it did before.
